text:
Alex M.: FYI — FinServX POC trying to reserve Dedicated capacity (4xA100) in eu-west-1 and provisioning is failing. Can we swarm? :eyes:
Emma R.: They're under a tight timeline. Contract signed, POC needs to run perf tests tomorrow. I asked them for expected QPS and peak tokens.
Priya K.: pinging infra team. Do we have the request id from the customer or the internal reservation id?
Emma R.: internal request id: rsrv-20240307-88a3. They tried via Console -> Dedicated -> Reservations -> Create. Error shown to customer: "Provisioning failed: Insufficient capacity in region"
infra-bot: [automated] Reservation attempt rsrv-20240307-88a3 -> FAILED. Error: CapacityNotAvailable: Requested GPU type a100, count 4 not available in eu-west-1 for requested window.
Samira (SRE): Noted. eu-west-1 has lower spare A100 pool this week. Two immediate options: 1) move to eu-central-1 or 2) use Dedicated + burst capacity (temporary shared nodes) while we try to free reserved units. Which does AE prefer?
Emma R.: FinServX explicitly requires eu-west-1 for data residency. They asked about bringing on-prem or VPC private deployment but want to avoid extra overhead during POC. Any way to make eu-west-1 happen?
Marco L.: We can attempt to satisfy with cross-region routing set to "region_preference": ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"] and enable strict residency via network ACLs — but if the reservation fails the runtime can fallback for compute while keeping data pinned via egress controls. Would need a quick change to reservation JSON and approval from security.
Priya K.: Can you paste the current reservation JSON? Also include the customer's workload profile (max_seq_len, avg_tokens/sec) so we can choose instance types and pre-warm caches.
Emma R.: Posting what the customer sent:
```
{
  "project": "finservx",
  "reservation_id": "rsrv-20240307-88a3",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "gpu_type": "a100",
  "count": 4,
  "start": "2024-03-08T09:00:00Z",
  "end": "2024-03-09T21:00:00Z",
  "autoscale": false
}
```
Customer workload: avg tokens/sec ~120, peak bursts up to 600 tokens/sec, main model is rlhf-heavy small-chat model (seq_len 2048).
Samira (SRE): With those numbers 4xA100 might be tight if they do bursts. Suggest autoscale true with max_count 8 and small cooldown. Also enable prefix KV cache for 90% of requests. That reduces load.
Marco L.: Proposed patched reservation:
```
{
  "region_preference": ["eu-west-1","eu-central-1"],
  "gpu_profile": {"preferred_type":"a100","fallback_type":"a10x"},
  "count": 4,
  "autoscale": {"enabled": true, "min": 4, "max": 8, "scale_policy": "latency_based"},
  "start": "2024-03-08T09:00:00Z"
}
```
This will attempt eu-west-1 first and fall back to eu-central-1 if capacity missing. We'll need a note in the SOW about ephemeral compute in eu-central-1 with data controls.
Priya K.: Security review: @Samira please confirm if fallback to eu-central-1 is acceptable if we restrict egress so customer data never leaves eu-west-1. If not acceptable, next step is to escalate capacity with cloud provider reserved inventory request (slow).
Samira (SRE): Fallback only works if we proxy model input/output through a data-plane in eu-west-1 (we can do that with VPC peering and relay nodes). That keeps PII in region but uses compute outside. It's allowed with customer's written consent.
Emma R.: I asked customer — they might accept compute in eu-central-1 as long as logs and raw payloads stay in eu-west-1. Can the platform ensure logs remain in-region?
Priya K.: Yes — set log_dest to s3://finservx-logs-eu-west-1 and disable replication. Also mask tokens at the edge.
infra-bot: Rate limit alert: 429 responses observed from staging endpoint during probe at 2024-03-07T14:11:23Z. Agents: reduce  parallel streams to 12 or enable request queuing.
Alex M.: The customer also reported intermittent 429 when running the perf harness (concurrency 40). Are we hitting API rate limits or internal per-VM socket limits?
Marco L.: Likely hitting per-instance connection limit + runtime request queue. Two quick fixes: 1) reduce parallel clients to 12-16 and enable continuous batching in runtime config, 2) increase instance count or enable autoscale.
Priya K.: I'll push a temporary runtime patch to increase concurrent request queue size from 256 -> 1024 for this reservation only. Patch command:
```
redwoodctl runtime patch --reservation rsrv-20240307-88a3 --set runtime.request_queue_size=1024
```
Apply with caution.
Samira (SRE): Also enable token-level cost guard to prevent runaway costs if autoscale triggers. Alert thresholds: cost/day > $2k triggers auto-throttle.
Emma R.: Pricing question from customer: what's cost delta if we enable autoscale to max 8 vs hard 4? Need estimate ASAP.
Alex M.: Quick ballpark from pricing book: 4xA100 reserved ~ $5.6k/day, burst to 8 maybe ~ $9.8k/day. Send formal quote via SalesOps.
infra-bot: [automated] Reservation rsrv-20240307-88a3 reattempt -> PENDING in eu-west-1 after runtime patch.
Samira (SRE): I coordinated with CloudOps — they freed one A100 node and revalidated quotas. We also set up the relay in eu-west-1 to keep logs/data pinned.
infra-bot: [automated] Reservation rsrv-20240307-88a3 -> ACTIVE (eu-west-1) at 2024-03-07T15:12:45Z.
Emma R.: :raised_hands: Great. I'll notify FinServX. Emma will confirm acceptance of fallback policy in writing and sign the addendum.
Alex M.: Thanks team for quick swarm. Follow-ups: Priya to leave autoscale enabled with min=4 max=8, Marco to monitor latency during perf run, Samira to verify logs retention.
Emma R.: I'll close this POC blocker thread once customer signs.
Marco L.: I'll drop a short runbook snippet into the ticket for next time (eu-west capacity hiccups). :memo:
Samira (SRE): Added alerting rule: "dedicated.region.capacity.low" -> paging on >2 consecutive failed reservations.
Emma R.: Customer updated: perf run successful, no PII left-region. They passed security checklist. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
